panels.figure_caption: Imaging features of periventricular nodular heterotopia (PVNH). PVNH patient: MRI T2-weighted (A), multiplanar reformation (MPR; B) and T2-weighted dark fluid (C) images reveal abnormal nodules of grey matter (PVNH) adjacent to the bilateral lateral ventricles (indicated by arrows).
in_text_mentions: linked neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by the presence of neuron clusters abnormally positioned near the ventricles rather than within the cortical layers where they would typically reside (Fig. 2). This aberrant neuronal positioning results from disruptions in the normal migration process during brain development, specifically from the ventricular zone to the cortex.64,65 Mutations in the FLNA gene are well-established causes of PVNH, typically resulting from the loss-of-function of one FLNA allele, leading to abnormal mRNA splicing or early truncation of the FLNA protein.66,67 For

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: MRI showing periventricular nodular heterotopia (arrowheads) which is consistent with the primary diagnosis. B: MRI showing additional periventricular nodular heterotopia (arrowheads) in patient. C: CT demonstrating widening of cerebral fissures and ventriculomegaly, which are structural findings associated with the patient's overall pathology. D: Sagittal MRI showing cerebral volume loss and structural anomalies consistent with the associated pathology of PNH.

panels.figure_caption: Brain MRI findings. (A,B) Periventricular nodular heterotopia (arrowheads) in patient; (C,D) Additional findings include small volume in the frontal and temporal lobes, prominent cerebral sulci and widened fissures, ventriculomegaly, and a thin corpus callosum.
in_text_mentions: Brain MRI revealed PNH, small volume in the frontal and temporal lobes, prominent cerebral sulci and widened fissures, ventriculomegaly and a thin corpus callosum (Figure 3). To assess the level of his development, we used GDS. The GDS revealed he had extremely severe global developmental delay in adaptation (14), large motor movement (18), fine motor movement (11), language (18), and personal-social development (19). Brainstem auditory evoked potentials revealed a delayed auditory conduction pathway (Figure 4). The result of the color Doppler ultrasound of the heart was unremarkable.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: The panel clearly shows bilateral nodular heterotopia in the periventricular region on T1 MRI, matching the article's subject and caption description. B: This panel shows the manual outlining of the nodules seen in Panel A, confirming their presence and location for volumetric analysis, linking directly to the diagnosis. C: This is a processed segmentation map of the gray matter derived from a patient exhibiting the target disease. While not a direct clinical photo, it is integral to characterizing the pathology. D: Similar to Panel C, this is a processed segmentation map of the white matter derived from the patient, supporting the radiological investigation of the disorder.

plate_findings.evidence: The ventricular lining (closed arrows and ovals) shows a bilateral nodular thickening.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a T2w MRI showing bilateral nodular thickening of the ventricular lining (arrows/ovals) following the grey matter, consistent with periventricular nodular heterotopia, as supported by the caption and article context. B: Panel B is a T2w MRI confirming the irregular lining and nodules following the grey matter, which is a classic sign of periventricular nodular heterotopia in a fetal brain. C: Panel C is an axial T1w MRI confirming the morphological features of the periventricular nodular heterotopia, consistent with the description provided.
panels.attribution_text: Thonissen et al. X-linked Bilateral Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia.. Journal of the Belgian Society of Radiology 2020. doi:10.5334/jbsr.2086. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Sagittal and axial T2w images (a, b) and axial T1w image (c) of the brain performed at a gestational age of 25 3/7 weeks. The ventricular lining (closed arrows and ovals) shows a bilateral nodular thickening following the signal intensities of the grey matter (open arrows).
in_text_mentions: An expert neurosonogram (Figure 1) at 25 weeks of GA demonstrated enlargement of the cisterna magna (thick arrows; 12 mm, normally <10 mm). Furthermore, an irregular lining of the lateral ventricles was noted on the axial and sagittal sections (ovals). Fetal MRI (Figure 2), performed three days later, confirmed the previously described irregular lining of the lateral ventricles (ovals and thin arrows) following the grey matter on T2- and T1-weighted images (open arrows) and enlarged cisterna magna. No additional anomalies were detected.

panels.figure_caption: Post-mortem axial and sagittal T2w (a, b) and axial T1w (c) MR images of the brain at a fetal age of 27 weeks. The ventricles are lined with multiple nodules (closed arrows and ovals) following the signal intensities of the grey matter (open arrows).
in_text_mentions: A multidisciplinary team approved the couple’s request for termination of pregnancy. A post-mortem MRI was performed at an age of 27 weeks and 6 days (Figure 3), within 2 hours after delivery. This examination clearly showed the periventricular nodules (closed arrows and ovals) with signal intensities following the grey matter (open arrows) on T2- and T1-weighted images, predominantly located next to the frontal horns and ventricular bodies on both sides. No additional anomalies were detected.

plate_findings.evidence: Brain MRI revealed bilateral, multiple periventricular nodular heterotopia (PNH) located at the dorsal pole of the frontal horn of the lateral ventricles.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Panel (a) shows an axial T1-weighted brain MRI demonstrating periventricular nodular heterotopia in an adolescent patient, matching the clinical description. b: Panel (b) shows a coronal brain MRI demonstrating periventricular nodular heterotopia in an adolescent patient, consistent with the clinical report. c: Panel (c) shows a sagittal brain MRI, illustrating multiple nodules along the lateral ventricular walls, which supports the diagnosis of PNH.
panels.attribution_text: Hoshi et al. Successful use of clozapine in a patient with schizophrenia comorbid with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and multiple periventricular nodular heterotopia: A case report.. PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences 2025. doi:10.1002/pcn5.70195. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (a–c) Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings. Brain MRI revealed bilateral, multiple periventricular nodular heterotopia (PNH) located at the dorsal pole of the frontal horn of the lateral ventricles. (a) Axial T1‐weighted image, (b) coronal view, and (c) sagittal view. The sagittal image (c) shows multiple PNHs along the lateral ventricular walls. The area circled in red indicates the locations of the PNHs.
in_text_mentions: At the age of 15, the patient was referred to our hospital and admitted for medical care. Due to persistent violent behavior, involuntary behavioral restrictions and isolation measures were required. A brain MRI scan was performed under sedation with flunitrazepam and revealed PNH (Figure 1). The results of genetic testing confirmed a deletion in the 22q11.2 region, consistent with 22q11.2 DS.

plate_findings.evidence: multiple subependymal nodular bilateral periventricular heterotopias

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (Panel 1, Panel 2, Panel 3). Panel 1: This MRI panel shows multiple subependymal nodules consistent with periventricular nodular heterotopia, as described in the article text during fetal development. Panel 2: This MRI panel demonstrates periventricular subependymal nodules, which are the hallmark finding for periventricular nodular heterotopia, within a fetal brain. Panel 3: This MRI panel shows the characteristic subependymal nodules associated with periventricular nodular heterotopia in a fetal patient.

plate_findings.evidence: MRI scan revealing periventricular nodules, consistent with PVNH.
MRI scan showing multiple gray matter nodules along the lateral ventricle body.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an MRI of a fetus showing periventricular nodules, a characteristic feature of Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia (PVNH), as confirmed by the article text. B: Panel B is an MRI of a fetus clearly demonstrating gray matter nodules extending along the ventricular body, directly supporting the diagnosis of PVNH mentioned in the context.
panels.attribution_text: Novillo-Del Álamo et al. Case Report and Literature Review-From Ultrasound to Genotype: Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia.. Case reports in obstetrics and gynecology 2025. doi:10.1155/crog/6563701. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Magnetic resonance performed during Week 29 of pregnancy.
in_text_mentions: A new MRI was performed in Week 29 in order to seek the evolution of the abnormalities (Figure 3). An ultrasound at 34 weeks of pregnancy revealed normal fetal growth and a normal fetal Doppler study. The fetal abnormalities, including PVNHs, bilateral ventriculomegaly, and atrioventricular valve dysplasia, remained stable compared to previous studies.

plate_findings.evidence: diffuse bilateral periventricular nodular heterotopia (yellow arrows)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Axial T1-weighted MRI showing reduced brain trophism and diffuse bilateral periventricular nodular heterotopia, matching the target disease. b: Axial T1-weighted MRI showing bilateral periventricular nodules indicative of the target disease. c: Sagittal MRI showing hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, which is a characteristic finding associated with this condition. d: Coronal T2-weighted MRI showing ventricular enlargement and dysmorphism secondary to the pathology.
panels.attribution_text: Andreoli et al. ARFGEF2-Related Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia: A Case Report and Literature Review.. NeuroSci 2026. doi:10.3390/neurosci7030063. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Axial (a,b) and sagittal (c) T1-weighted images and coronal T2-weighted images (d), showing reduced brain trophism, diffuse bilateral periventricular nodular heterotopia (yellow arrows), thin corpus callosum (c), and dysmorphic and enlarged ventricles.
in_text_mentions: lay with poor head control and minimal vocalisation. Neurological examination revealed tetraparesis, with hypotonia predominantly affecting the lower limbs. Reduced growth parameters were also observed (weight 7.8 kg, <3rd percentile; height 71 cm, 3rd–10th percentile; head circumference 44 cm, 3rd percentile). Brain MRI revealed reduced brain trophism, extensive bilateral and symmetrical subependymal heterotopic nodules along the walls of the lateral ventricles, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, dysmorphic and enlarged lateral ventricles, and incomplete eversion of the hippocampi (Figure 1).
